beats.text: Likes change what you like. And your brain can't help it.
UCLA researchers showed thirty-two teens an Instagram-style feed inside a brain scanner. But there was a trick.
The researchers set the likes themselves. Same photo, lots of likes or just a few.
With lots of likes, teens were more likely to like it too. Even their own photos.
And the brain's reward center lit up more for the popular ones.
So you don't just like what's good. You like what's already liked.

sources: Sherman, Payton, Hernandez, Greenfield & Dapretto (2016), 'The Power of the Like in Adolescence: Effects of Peer Influence on Neural and Behavioral Responses to Social Media', Psychological Science 27(7). 32 teens aged 13-18, fMRI, 148 photos incl. 40 own; like counts assigned by the researchers. More likely to like photos with many likes (incl. own photos); greater nucleus accumbens (reward) activity for photos with many likes. Via UCLA / Neuroscience News (2016).
ask: DO YOU CHECK THE LIKES FIRST?
